name: dYdX V3
rootCause: On July 23, the dydx.exchange domain was discovered to have been compromised. The attacker changed the DNS Nameservers from Cloudflare to DDoS-Guard. The attacker also successfully removed the DNSSEC settings on the domain. The attacker hosted a malicious site which requested that any connected wallets transfer ETH and other ERC20 tokens to the attacker’s Ethereum address. Two users were affected, resulting in a loss of approximately $31,000.

On July 23, 2024, dYdX V3's frontend was hijacked via a DNS attack, redirecting users to a phishing site. Two users lost a total of approximately $31,000 after interacting with the fake interface. The backend smart contracts were unaffected, and dYdX quickly restored domain control. The incident was caused by a DNS nameserver hijacking following a registrar migration, allowing attackers to disable DNSSEC and redirect dydx.exchange to a phishing frontend. This exposed visiting users to malicious wallet connection prompts and token approval requests.

Crypto exchange dYdX has announced that the website for their v3 exchange was compromised, and is urging people not to use it. This announcement came almost simultaneously with a report from Bloomberg that the company behind the exchange was looking to sell the software behind the v3 exchange, after they’d upgraded to what they call v4. The affected domain was hosted on Squarespace, which could connect this compromise to similar events earlier in the month affecting domains registered there.
